domestic.debt_note: Last MTB auction 2026-07-08: govt raised Rs2,067.9bn vs a Rs2.4tn target; cutoffs eased across the curve -- 1M 11.3968% (-40.3bps), 3M 11.3978% (-35.2bps), 6M 11.4375% (-31bps), 12M 11.4880% (-35bps), all sub the 11.5% policy rate, signalling market pricing of an eventual rate cut (https://propakistani.pk/2026/07/08/govt-borrows-rs-2-trillion-from-local-debt-market/). PIB 10Y last read 11.69% on 2026-07-06, down 0.03pp on the session and down 1.06pp over the trailing month (https://tradingeconomics.com/pakistan/government-bond-yield). SBP-held reserves fell $1.245bn (-6.7% w/w) to $17.226bn as of week ended 2026-07-10, down from $18.471bn on 2026-07-03, on external debt repayments; total liquid reserves $22.676bn, down from $23.988bn the prior week (https://tribune.com.pk/story/2618658/reserves-down-124b-on-debt-repayments, https://www.dawn.com/news/2016021/sbp-reserves-fall-12bn). Government is reportedly weighing reactivating a 2026 austerity package (four-day work week, official-vehicle/travel cuts) explicitly citing the reserve drawdown -- a real-time domestic fiscal-stress signal (https://propakistani.pk/2026/07/16/sbp-reserves-crash-after-big-debt-payment/).
domestic.remittances: FY26 closed at a record $41.6bn (+9% YoY); June 2026 alone $3.5bn (+2% YoY, -18% MoM off a high May base). No new print found this run (https://www.dawn.com/news/2014313/remittances-hit-record-416bn-in-fy26)
domestic.current_account: June 2026 posted a ~$650mn deficit vs a May surplus, tipping FY26 to a small full-year deficit versus FY25's $1.84bn surplus. No new print found this run (https://www.dawn.com/news/2016376)

global_read: global.json (17:36) shows Brent $88.58 (+0.54% 1d, +13.71% 1mo), S&P -1.01%/Dow -0.77% both red, VIX 18.2 easing -3.04% 1d but still +5.32% 1mo, PKR/USD flat at 277.73, DXY 100.89 (+0.14% 1d). Read: equities red, oil elevated and climbing on a still-live US-Iran/Strait of Hormuz conflict (confirmed again this run via a dedicated Wikipedia tracking page '2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis' and news of the prior truce breaking down on 2026-07-08 with Brent spiking as high as $80.59 intraday that day, since extending further toward/above $88-90 -- see drivers). VIX easing even as the conflict is live suggests the tape has not yet fully repriced escalation risk. Net: global backdrop is a clear headwind for PSX today, oil the dominant transmission channel via the import bill and PKR.
drivers: SBP policy rate held at 11.5% at the 2026-06-15 MPC (final FY26 review); MPC cited a 3.7% FY26 GDP growth estimate and reserves rising to $17.2bn as of June 5 on IMF EFF/RSF disbursements; medium-term inflation target remains 5-7% (https://www.thenews.pk/story/1420738-sbp-maintains-115-policy-rate-in-final-fy26-review, https://www.sbp.org.pk/press/2026/Pr-15-Jun-2026.pdf). Next MPC (first of FY27) confirmed for 2026-07-27 (https://www.momentumpakistan.com/blog/breaking-sbps-first-monetary-policy-fy27-on-july-27-transparency-boost-2026-06-23-18-01-45-gpmsiudorh-52609)

CPI eased to 11.1% YoY in June 2026 from 11.7% in May (still up sharply from 3.2% in June 2025); urban 11.2%, rural 10.9%; MoM CPI actually fell 0.3%; FY26 average inflation 7.05% vs 4.49% in FY25 (https://www.brecorder.com/news/40428026/pakistan-inflation-hits-111-in-june-2026, https://www.pbs.gov.pk/monthly-inflation-report-for-june-2026/)

IMF EFF/RSF program on track: 3rd EFF review + 2nd RSF review completed 2026-05-08, disbursing ~$1.1bn (EFF) + ~$220mn (RSF), bringing cumulative disbursements to ~$4.8bn; FY26 primary surplus of 1.6% of GDP reported in line with targets (https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2026/05/08/pr-26147-pakistan-imf-completes-3rd-rev-of-extended-arrangement-under-eff-and-2nd-rev-arrang-rsf)

SBP FX reserves fell $1.245bn w/w to $17.226bn (week ended 2026-07-10) on external debt repayments, down from $18.471bn the prior week; total liquid reserves $22.676bn, down from $23.988bn -- consistent, cross-confirmed reserve-stress signal (https://tribune.com.pk/story/2618658/reserves-down-124b-on-debt-repayments, https://propakistani.pk/2026/07/16/sbp-reserves-crash-after-big-debt-payment/)

Latest T-bill auction (2026-07-08): govt raised Rs2,067.9bn vs a Rs2.4tn target; cutoffs eased 31-40bps across tenors to 1M 11.3968%/3M 11.3978%/6M 11.4375%/12M 11.4880%, all below the 11.5% policy rate -- market pricing in an eventual cut despite the reserve/oil stress (https://propakistani.pk/2026/07/08/govt-borrows-rs-2-trillion-from-local-debt-market/)

Ongoing US-Iran/Strait of Hormuz conflict remains the dominant external risk transmission channel: a dedicated Wikipedia tracker ('2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis') and multiple wire pieces confirm the earlier truce broke down around 2026-07-08 (Brent spiking to $80.59 intraday that day) with tensions continuing to escalate since, keeping Brent on an upward path (global.json shows $88.58, +13.7% 1mo) -- this directly pressures Pakistan's import bill, PKR and the SBP's coming 2026-07-27 rate decision (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Strait_of_Hormuz_crisis, https://www.spglobal.com/energy/en/news-research/latest-news/crude-oil/070826-factbox-oil-futures-pass-80b-as-us-iran-ceasefire-appears-to-collapse)

Government reportedly weighing reactivation of an austerity package (four-day work week, official-vehicle/foreign-travel cuts) explicitly tied to the reserve drawdown -- a domestic fiscal-stress signal still at the deliberation stage (https://propakistani.pk/2026/07/16/sbp-reserves-crash-after-big-debt-payment/)

PSX itself has been volatile on the conflict headlines this month -- a >6,400-point single-day plunge on renewed US-Iran hostilities was reported by multiple outlets, alongside separate sessions of sharp rebounds, underscoring two-way, headline-driven volatility rather than a clean trend (https://profit.pakistantoday.com.pk/2026/07/14/psx-plunges-over-5200-points-as-us-iran-tensions-rising-oil-prices-trigger-heavy-sell-off, https://www.dawn.com/news/2015872/psx-stages-strong-recovery-as-kse-100-index-gains-2800-points)
